name: Cloud City Boba Fett
note: Only came in the 2003 Cloud City set, and its printed arms and legs make it one of the most valuable minifigures ever.

name: Chrome Gold C-3PO
note: Hidden in 10,000 random sets for Star Wars' 30th anniversary; the chrome scratches easily, so flawless ones sell for much more.

name: White Boba Fett
note: A 2010 promotional giveaway made to look like an early prototype; still-sealed bags fetch the highest prices.

name: Darth Vader
note: Appears in dozens of sets, so most versions are cheap, but early ones with special printing are worth more.

name: Stormtrooper
note: One of the most produced minifigures ever, so prices stay low unless it's a rare variant.

name: Luke Skywalker (Tatooine)
note: Included in many sets; having his lightsaber and hair piece makes a small difference.

name: Harry Potter (Hogwarts Robes)
note: Comes in lots of current sets, so it's easy to find and inexpensive.

name: Hermione Granger
note: A common figure; complete ones with her wand sell a little higher.

name: Rubeus Hagrid
note: His big-figure body only appears in a few sets, which keeps his price above regular figures.

name: Professor Quirrell
note: The original 2001 version has Voldemort's face printed on the back of his head, which collectors love.

name: Viktor Krum
note: Only came with the 2005 Durmstrang Ship set, so he's hard to find today.

name: Iron Man
note: There are many armor versions; newer common ones are cheap while early ones cost more.

name: Spider-Man
note: Very common in recent sets; condition of the face and leg printing matters most.

name: Phoenix (Comic-Con Exclusive)
note: Given away in small numbers at San Diego Comic-Con, so sealed ones are especially valuable.

name: Batman
note: Batman comes in many sets, so most versions are inexpensive.

name: Wonder Woman
note: A common figure; including her lasso and tiara adds a little value.

name: Bizarro (Comic-Con Exclusive)
note: A San Diego Comic-Con giveaway; the original packaging and card matter a lot for value.

name: Kai
note: The original red ninja was re-released many times, which keeps prices low.

name: Lloyd
note: The green ninja shows up in lots of sets and is easy to find.

name: Golden Ninja Lloyd
note: His shiny gold printing wears off easily, so clean ones are worth more.

name: Police Officer
note: City figures are made in huge numbers, so they're usually just a few dollars.

name: Firefighter
note: Common and easy to find; a matching helmet and air tank help a little.

name: Mr. Gold
note: Only 5,000 were hidden in Series 10 blind bags, and the value jumps if it still has its numbered certificate.

name: Lady Liberty
note: A popular Series 6 figure; she needs her torch and tablet to be complete.

name: Banana Guy
note: A fan favorite from Series 16, but plenty were made so it stays affordable.

name: Gandalf the Grey
note: The 2012 version is worth more than the newer 2023 one from Rivendell; his hat and staff are a must.

name: Frodo Baggins
note: Appeared in several sets; versions with the One Ring and Sting are worth a bit more.

name: Witch-king of Angmar
note: Only came in a couple of sets, and his crown and sword are often missing.

name: Gollum
note: His special small body makes him stand out; the 2012 version and the newer 2024 one sell for different prices.

name: Red Classic Spaceman
note: Lots were made, but a crack-free helmet and a crisp space logo on the chest raise the price.

name: Blue Classic Spaceman
note: Fewer were made than the red and white ones, and worn chest logos lower the value.
